tip: 'Ska säljas' = will be sold: 'ska' plus a verb ending in -s gives a future passive. Very common in real estate.
The -s ending can mark a passive, but 'träffas' here is not passive: it means meet each other, not is met.
'Liknas' takes 'vid', not 'av', for the thing compared to: 'hon liknas vid sin mamma' = she is likened to her mother.
'Turas om' means take turns. It is a set phrase: 'turas om att laga mat' = take turns cooking.
'Skulle vilja' is the polite would like, softer than 'vill' (want): 'jag skulle vilja ha en kaffe'.
'Överraskande' (surprising) is the -ande form of the verb and never changes: one form fits every noun and number.
For a hypothetical, use past tense after 'om' (if) and 'skulle' in the result: 'om vi hade pengar skulle vi resa'.
'Hoppas' (to hope) always ends in -s but has active meaning – the -s is part of the verb, not a passive.
In a passive, 'av' names the doer, like English by: 'godkändes av chefen' = approved by the boss.
'Bli' plus a form like 'stulen' (stolen) is a second passive: 'blev stulen' stresses a single completed event, unlike the -s passive.
'Andas' (to breathe) always ends in -s but is active in meaning – the -s is part of the verb, not a passive.
'Brottas' = wrestle; the -s ending means they do it to each other.
'Fattas' takes the missed person as its subject: 'han fattas mig' = he is missing to me, so I miss him.
The -s ending plus 'åt' means doing it together: 'vi följdes åt' = we went along with each other.
'Umgås' exists only in the -s form and means to spend time together. There is no plain 'umgå': 'vi umgås' = we socialize.
Use 'det finns' for both there is and there are, whatever the number: 'det finns många sjöar' = there are many lakes.
The -s ending can form a passive, and 'av' marks the doer: 'jag berörs av musiken' = I am touched by the music.
'Skulle kunna' plus a verb means could or would be able to: 'jag skulle kunna hjälpa' = I could help.
'Kommer att' plus a verb is the plain future: 'det kommer att bli dyrt' = it will be expensive.
'Visar sig' means turns out or proves to be, and the 'sig' is required: 'det visar sig vara sant' = it turns out to be true.
For would have, use 'skulle ha' plus the same verb form as after 'har': 'skulle inte ha gjort' = would not have done.
When a phrase like 'i gengäld' (in return) opens the clause, the verb still comes second and the subject follows: 'i gengäld hjälper jag'.
'Halv fem' means half to five, that is 4:30, not 5:30 – Swedish counts toward the coming hour.
'Lyckas' ends in -s but is active, not passive: 'vi lyckas' = we succeed, not we are succeeded. It only exists in this -s form.
Front a word like 'däremot' and the verb moves ahead of the subject: 'däremot gillar jag', not 'däremot jag gillar'.
'Oroa sig' (to worry) takes a pronoun that tracks the subject: with 'du' you say 'oroa dig', with 'jag' it is 'oroa mig'.
'Kommer att bli' = will become/get. 'Bli' is the go-to verb for changes of state.
The -s on 'ses' means see each other. The same trick gives 'träffas' (meet) and 'hörs' (talk soon).
'Skulle' plus a bare verb like 'göra' expresses would, a hypothetical: 'han skulle göra det', not something he actually did.
'Skulle ha stannat' covers both a neutral would have stayed and a regretful should have stayed. Context tells you which is meant.
